nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, two words $u$ and $v$ over an alphabet are $k$-abelian equivalent when $k \ge 1$, both $u$ and $v$ are nonempty, $u$ and $v$ have the same prefix of length $k - 1$ and the same suffix of length $k - 1$ (a word shorter than $k - 1$ counting as its own prefix and suffix), and every word $t$ of length $k$ occurs as a factor of $u$, counting overlapping occurrences, exactly as often as it…
nodes.title: $k$-abelian equivalence

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a finite word $w$ is $k$-abelian square-free when $k \ge 1$ and no factor of $w$ (a word $x$ with $w = pxs$ for some words $p$ and $s$) is a $k$-abelian square.
nodes.title: $k$-abelian square-free words

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a word $w$ is a $k$-abelian square when $w = uv$ for two nonempty words $u$ and $v$ that are $k$-abelian equivalent.
nodes.title: $k$-abelian squares

nodes.summary: Two words $u$ and $v$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ are $3$-abelian equivalent when they are $k$-abelian equivalent for $k = 3$: both are nonempty, they have the same prefix and the same suffix of length $2$ (a shorter word counting as its own prefix and suffix), and every word of length $3$ occurs as a factor of $u$, counting overlapping occurrences, exactly as often as it occurs in $v$.
nodes.title: $3$-abelian equivalence of ternary words

nodes.summary: A finite word $w$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is $3$-abelian square-free when no factor of $w$ (a word $x$ with $w = pxs$ for some words $p$ and $s$) is a $3$-abelian square.
nodes.title: $3$-abelian square-free ternary words

nodes.summary: A word $w$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is a $3$-abelian square when $w = uv$ for two nonempty words $u$ and $v$ that are $3$-abelian equivalent.
nodes.title: $3$-abelian squares over a ternary alphabet

nodes.summary: For words $w$ and $t$ over an alphabet with $t$ nonempty, the factor count of $t$ in $w$ is the number of positions of $w$ at which an occurrence of $t$ starts, overlapping occurrences all being counted. The factor count of the empty word is $0$.
nodes.title: Number of occurrences of a factor

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
